release.title: Bilateral Deficiency: Residual SAT Optimisation and Independent Domination in Regular-DIM Graphs

status_semantics.asserted_in_candidate: A claim accompanied by a written proof or the explicitly identified finite evidence. It is not a peer-review or acceptance status.
status_semantics.checked_finite_claim: A finite claim whose packaged inputs and certificate or exhaustive computation have been replayed by the producer-side workflow.
status_semantics.formally_checked_finite_claim: A finite proposition checked through the identified Lean path. The label does not extend to the universal theory or its file-to-proposition translation obligations.

claims.claim: Bilateral deficiency has an intrinsic bipolar-residual formulation and is represented by a size-preserving bijection with independent dominating sets of the formula graph, including the solution-polynomial identity.
claims.scope: Finite indexed CNF formulas under the definitions in the manuscript.
claims.boundary: Universal written mathematics; not proof-assistant formalised or independently reviewed.

claims.claim: Bilateral deficiency is additive under variable-disjoint conjunction, supports width lifting and replication, recovers the stated MaxSAT quantity under replication, and has the stated width-sensitive complexity boundary.
claims.scope: The constructions and decision problems exactly defined in the manuscript.
claims.boundary: Tests are conformance checks and do not replace the universal written proofs.

claims.claim: For a finite simple regular graph equipped with a dominating induced matching and its associated indexed formula, the gap satisfies i(G)-mu*(G)=beta(F).
claims.scope: Regular graphs equipped with a dominating induced matching, under the coordinatisation in the manuscript.
claims.boundary: The identity is not asserted for arbitrary regular graphs without the stated DIM structure.

claims.claim: For every simple d-regular graph equipped with a dominating induced matching, the stated constructive replacement inequality holds; for d=3 this gives i(G) <= mu*(G)+floor(mu*(G)/6).
claims.scope: Finite simple d-regular graphs equipped with a dominating induced matching.
claims.boundary: This is a written universal proof, not a formal proof-assistant result.

claims.claim: For every connected cubic skeleton R, the connected edge-cover amplifier A(R) satisfies beta(A(R))=rho(R)=|V(R)|-nu(R), yielding connected cubic-DIM families with linear gap and construction-specific asymptotic density 1/72 from the imported O--West equality family.
claims.scope: The amplifier construction in the manuscript; the 1/72 sharpness is only within this construction.
claims.boundary: The universal amplifier theorem and imported matching theorem are not formalised or independently re-proved.

claims.claim: Order 50 is the minimum among finite simple cubic graphs admitting a dominating induced matching for which i(G)>mu*(G), and the motivating connected example attains order 50.
claims.scope: Cubic graphs admitting a dominating induced matching.
claims.boundary: No minimum-order claim is made outside the DIM class; the imported 20-clause theorem is not independently re-proved.

claims.claim: The motivating 15-variable, 20-clause indexed formula has bilateral deficiency exactly 1.
claims.boundary: The DIMACS parser and file-to-proposition translation remain trusted boundaries; this does not formalise the universal definition or bijection.

claims.claim: The attributed SAT 2024 enforcer composition and the connected occurrence switch each have bilateral deficiency exactly 1.
claims.scope: The byte-identified finite formulas and threshold encodings recorded in their receipts.
claims.boundary: The 5,793,599,477-byte connected-switch LRAT is an extended object; its absence from the compact archive does not weaken the separate written amplifier theorem.

claims.claim: For the visibly transcribed ten-clause enforcer, the complete finite terminal signature is exactly (0,empty,0), (1,empty,1), (*,empty,1), and (*,{-},1).
claims.scope: All 3^8=6,561 partial assignments of the hard-coded eight-variable clause list.
claims.boundary: The visible clause transcription is the translation boundary; the source formula and its attribution remain imported.

claims.claim: The packaged beta<=0 threshold encoding of the motivating formula matches an independently reconstructed symbolic encoding and passes the declared exhaustive small-formula semantic corpus.
claims.scope: The named encoding, map, seven-case corpus, and 66 constrained ternary-state checks in the receipt.
claims.boundary: This is producer-side clean-room validation, not independent reproduction, external review, or proof-assistant verification of the compiler.

open_claims.claim: Determine the exact cubic-DIM extremal constants.
Determine the sign complexity on proper simple exact signed-occurrence (3,2,2)-CNF.
Determine the minimum counterexample order among cubic graphs outside the DIM class.
